profile.headline: Scientific Software Developer @ CSS | Atmospheric Sciences, Meteorology

positions.title: Scientific Software Developer
positions.locationName: Silver Spring, Maryland, United States · Remote
positions.description:
Red Tide Respiratory Irritation Forecast (RIF) Model
++Presented Poster at NEIWPCC’s 12th U S. Symposium on Harmful Algae Portland ME
+Presented Poster at 23rd Symposium on the Coastal Environment at the 105th AMS Annual Meeting
+Launched NCCOS-side concept development page for Gulf of Mexico HAB Forecasts
+Co-developed and maintains Team documentation built in HTML
+Developed and maintains database for HAB Forecasting Branch
+Standardize, archive and maintain forecast data inputs and outputs
+Special recognition by Tim Gallaudet, Ph.D., Rear Admiral, U.S. Navy (Ret.) Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Oceans and Atmosphere / Deputy NOAA Administrator, Acting Under Secretary of Commerce for Oceans and Atmosphere / NOAA Administrator for HABscope project Nov 2018
+Complete transfor of existing Toxic Wind Model code to accept new inputs, output respiratory forecasts and run every 3-hrs as the Respiratory Irritation Forecast (RIF) Model
+Successfully integrated real-time Pinellas County, FL data sets into the forecast python scripts under a tight deadline despite setbacks, recognized with 2018 NCCOS Peer Recognition Special Achievement Award.
+Collaborated and worked concurrently with Gulf of Mexico Coastal Ocean Observing System (GCOOS) partners to launch live public-facing website Oct 2018.
+Lake Erie HAB Transition
+Successfully worked across a dual-platform Windows/Linux-based environment and navigated dual-office effort between NCCOS and CO-OPS to facilitate Lake Erie Harmful Algae Bloom ecological forecast transition from NCCOS research system to CO-OPS operational system
+Upgraded LE HAB ecological forecast to ⅓ of previous time with a newly created semi-automated Python scripting processes
+Created numerous scripts for comparison between the two analyst teams to improve transition accuracy
+Completed LE HAB Transition project in a little over half the allotted time, exceptional work recognized with Team Member of the Year award Nov 2016

positions.title: Meteorology Adjunct Faculty Member
positions.description:
+Recognized with Montgomery College Outstanding Part-Time Faculty Award for Excellence in Teaching for the academic year 2019-2020
+Creative learning techniques to reintegrate concepts, non-traditional instruction and utilization of technology
+Successfully and uniquely transitioned AOSC100, AOSC105 and AOSC105L to Structured Remote Learning
+Utilized MS PowerPoint/Google Slides and MS Word/Google Docs in Lecture and lab practicals for Introduction to Meteorology course
+Included strong scientific and technical writing assignments component of course
+Co-facilitated new curriculum development of new labs and syllabus materials for AOSC 100 and 105 courses
positions.insights: Skills: Attention to Detail · Google Drive · Curriculum Development · Climate · Google Docs · Online Teaching · Meteorology · Geography · University Teaching · Creativity and Innovation · Google Workspace · Follow-through Skills · Google Slides

positions.title: Podcast Host
positions.description:
• Produced and edited over 48 episodes focused on weather, climate, and earth science.  
• Developed engaging content that catered to diverse audiences, including two all-Spanish episodes.  
• Collaborated with experts to explore varying topics, enhancing public understanding of environmental issues.
positions.insights: Skills: Creative Writing · Audio Recording · Research Skills · Research · Audio Editing

positions.title: Faculty Research Assistant
positions.description:
+Worked in both a Windows and Linux-based environment to facilitate large data downloads
+Processed MODIS Landcover and VCF satellite remote sensing data to Climate Model matching parameters for NASA ACCESS project, working with PNNL, prepared technical documents for methodology, created and presented posters for scientific meetings
+Repackaged HDF and NetCDF data to more geographical sciences ready data format, GeoTiff (including embedding metadata and color tables)
+Found previous Geographical position UMD Tile system error and corrected for future datasets
+Edited manuscripts for co-workers within working group
+Performed literature reviews for multiple projects
+Answered public queries for Global Land Cover Facility (GLCF) data
+Multitasked to complete projects with overlapping deadlines
+Updated GLCF website using HTML scripting and Javascript
positions.insights: Skills: HTML Scripting · Computer-literate performer · Attention to Detail · Data Processing · Reason · Research Skills · Public Relations · Software Development · JavaScript · Linux · Technical Writing · Manuscript Editing · Remote Sensing · Follow-through Skills · Poster Presentations · Satellite Imagery

positions.title: Research Analyst
positions.description:
+Worked in a Linux-based environment to perform geospatial analysis on an assortment of research topics including long-term vegetation dynamics, interactions between inter-annual climate/rainfall variability, land surface temperature and vegetation both at global and continental scales and climate-disease teleconnections
+Processed and analyzed AVHRR and MODIS satellite remote sensing data (including data quality control flags) using IDL for research projects leading to publication
+Edited manuscripts on several occasions leading to publication
+Performed literature review for published scientific journal articles
+Presented poster at numerous scientific poster sessions on vegetation dynamics relationship to disease outbreaks
+Co-mentored research and edited manuscript of student intern in analysis of MODIS land surface temperature data
